This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

Silly String became a counter-IED tool because it’s light, keeps its shape, and can reveal hidden tripwires. Marines would stand outside a suspected room, shake a can, then spray inside: if the string hits the ground, there’s no tripwire; if it stays floating, a hard-to-see wire may be keeping it up. It’s light enough that if it contacts a wire, it wouldn’t have the force needed to trigger the device, and it can also stick slightly to the wire so soldiers know where it is. Silly String can’t detect pressure plates or electronic detonators, though. What other counter-IED tricks should we cover next?
